ambiguities: The dream image ('j'avais rêvé que Charlus avait cent dix ans... de Mme Verdurin, qu'elle avait acheté cinq milliards un bouquet de violettes') is explicitly framed by the narrator as evidence of the impossibility and depth of his sleep ('rêvé à rebours de mes notions de la veille et de toutes les possibilités de la vie courante'), not as a real evaluative claim about Mme Verdurin's extravagance; it is treated here as immaterial dream-logic rather than a scorable appraisal event, though a reader could see it as a comic caricature of her ostentation.

The narrator's remark that his mother 'ne pouvait comprendre l'assiduité de Charlus chez les Verdurin' and the aside about secretly commissioning Albertine's hat as a surprise are both hypothetical/incidental (introduced via 'j'aurais bien étonné ma mère, si je lui avais raconté...') and do not stage either the mother or Albertine in an actual local social interaction with a clear outcome, so neither was scored.
